title: merge-janitor: timeout 1800 lacks -k; TERM-ignoring janitor session wedges the janitor forever
description: Same hazard class as 7mvj (fixed in sync-beads-workers.sh as timeout -k 10 900): scripts/merge-janitor.sh:33 runs 'timeout 1800 opencode run' without -k. A janitor LLM session that ignores SIGTERM hangs the janitor forever, and its surviving grandchildren keep writing the worktree after rc=124. Fix mirrors 7mvj: timeout -k <grace> 1800 (grace ~10s), and update the log line to document rc 137 (TERM ignored then KILLed) alongside 124. NOTE: the janitor's session also lacks the d42k git-state pin entirely (no HEAD/ref/MERGE_HEAD snapshot around its LLM call) — consider whether it needs one; that is a bigger, separate hardening question worth scoping when this bead is worked.
close_reason: Already fixed on main before this bead was filed. Commit d60aa22692 (worker1, Sep 8 19:30) applied the exact 7mvj-mirror the bead asks for: scripts/merge-janitor.sh resolve_file() now runs 'timeout -k 10 1800' with the matching comment and the log line 'budget=1800s+10s-kill-grace exit=$rc (124=timeout, 137=TERM ignored then KILLed)'. The -k 10 grace escalates a TERM-ignoring session to KILL (rc 137), so the janitor cannot wedge forever. This worker's branch (beads-worker-5) simply predates d60aa's merge-base, so its working tree shows the old code — no new change needed. The separate hardening question the bead raises (no git-state pin around the janitor's LLM call) is tracked by nm0h/840r/0mqr family, out of scope here.
